choices.label: C
choices.text: Bloodborne spread through reused intravenous tubing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contaminated surfaces and the hands of health care workers

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fecal-oral spread from an asymptomatic kitchen worker

explanation.summary: Acinetobacter spreads readily on contaminated surfaces and health care workers' hands, and it can colonize patients for months.
explanation.whyCorrect: Although Acinetobacter is not considered normal flora, it can colonize patients for months after an infection. It is easily transmitted through contaminated surfaces or the hands of health care workers, which is why it causes hospital outbreaks. Infections are most common in the intensive care unit among patients with severe comorbidities and immunosuppression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cooling tower aerosols are the classic route for Legionella pneumophila.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Airborne nuclei describe organisms such as tuberculosis, not Acinetobacter.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Reuse of intravenous tubing is not the described mechanism of Acinetobacter spread.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fecal-oral transmission describes enteric pathogens and does not explain an ICU outbreak of this organism.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas aeruginosa possesses lipopolysaccharide, a polysaccharide capsule, pili, and a flagellum. Which of the following functions is attributable specifically to its flagellum?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adherence of the bacterium to plastic surfaces

choices.label: B
choices.text: Formation of the extracellular biofilm matrix

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inhibition of host cell protein synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: Movement of the bacterium through its environment

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sequestration of free iron from host tissue

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas is motile by a single polar flagellum.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas species are gram-negative bacilli that are motile by a single polar flagellum, visible on electron microscopy as one long appendage at one pole. Motility is the function of this structure and is one of the features that distinguishes Pseudomonas from the non-motile Acinetobacter.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adherence to surfaces is the job of pili, not the flagellum.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The biofilm matrix is built from secreted extracellular polysaccharides and other macromolecules.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Inhibition of host protein synthesis is the action of exotoxin A.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Iron sequestration is performed by the pigment pyoverdine.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is not considered part of the normal human flora, yet exposure to it is essentially unavoidable. Which of the following best describes where this organism is typically found?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Soil and water, including moist hospital environments

choices.label: B
choices.text: The axillary and groin skin as resident flora

choices.label: C
choices.text: The colon of healthy adults as a minor commensal

choices.label: D
choices.text: The gastric mucosa beneath the mucus layer

choices.label: E
choices.text: The nasopharynx of asymptomatic child carriers

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas is an environmental organism of soil and water rather than a member of normal flora.
explanation.whyCorrect: P. aeruginosa is not considered normal flora but is commonly found in soil and water. Members of the genus are extremely adaptable and produce a broad range of enzymes that let them survive in very adverse conditions with minimal nutrients. They are so tough that antimicrobial hand sanitizers and cleaning products are recalled frequently because of Pseudomonas contamination, meaning the organism can thrive in substances meant to kill bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Resident skin flora includes staphylococci and corynebacteria, not Pseudomonas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas is explicitly not considered normal flora of the gastrointestinal tract.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The gastric mucus layer is the niche of Helicobacter pylori.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nasopharyngeal carriage describes organisms such as S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Most Pseudomonas species are obligate aerobes, yet a deep, walled-off abscess with a poor oxygen supply grows Pseudomonas on culture. Which of the following best explains this finding?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Biofilm formation permits growth without any metabolism

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pyocyanin allows the organism to generate its own oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some Pseudomonas species can grow as facultative anaerobes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The alginate capsule traps oxygen inside the abscess cavity

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organism forms endospores that germinate without oxygen

explanation.summary: Although most Pseudomonas species are obligate aerobes, some are facultative anaerobes and can cause anaerobic infections such as abscesses.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas species are gram-negative bacilli that are motile by a single polar flagellum, and most are obligate aerobes. Some species, however, are facultatively anaerobic. It is these species that can cause anaerobic infections such as abscesses.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Biofilms shelter bacteria but do not remove the requirement for metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pyocyanin is a cytotoxic blue pigment and does not generate oxygen.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Alginate forms a water-binding mucoid capsule and does not supply oxygen to the abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas does not form endospores; that is a feature of Bacillus and Clostridium species.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas recovered from an indwelling catheter is embedded within a slimy layer of secreted extracellular polysaccharides and other macromolecules. Which of the following best describes the advantage this layer confers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Conversion of the organism to an intracellular pathogen

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct inhibition of host cell protein synthesis machinery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enhanced swimming motility along the catheter surface

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased rate of bacterial replication within host tissues

choices.label: E
choices.text: Survival in harsh environments, including the host immune response

explanation.summary: Biofilms are slimy barriers that protect Pseudomonas from the environment and from the host immune response.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas species are exceptionally good at forming biofilms. By secreting extracellular polysaccharides and other macromolecules they create slimy barriers that let them survive harsh environments, and inside a patient those barriers shield them from the host immune response. This ability, combined with their tolerance for artificial surfaces such as catheters and endotracheal tubes, underlies much of their success in hospitals.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pseudomonas remains an extracellular pathogen within the biofilm.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Inhibition of host protein synthesis is the action of exotoxin A, not of the biofilm matrix.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The biofilm anchors bacteria in place rather than enhancing their swimming motility.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Biofilm-embedded bacteria are typically slow growing; faster replication is not the advantage.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 16-year-old steps on a nail that penetrates the sole of his sneaker into his foot. Ten days later he has deep, localized foot pain, and magnetic resonance imaging shows osteomyelitis of the calcaneus. Which of the following is the most likely causal organism?

explanation.summary: Puncture wounds through a shoe can inoculate Pseudomonas into deep tissue and cause osteomyelitis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas can cause skin and soft tissue infection, especially when trauma or immunosuppression is present. Piercing injuries such as stepping on a nail introduce the bacteria into deep tissue and can lead to bone and joint infection. Green pus at such a site is a further clue that Pseudomonas is the causative agent.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Clostridium tetani causes tetanus with spastic paralysis, not a localized bone infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Haemophilus influenzae is a respiratory pathogen and is not associated with puncture wounds.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes septic arthritis in the context of disseminated gonococcal infection, not nail puncture osteomyelitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Streptococcus pyogenes causes superficial cellulitis and erysipelas rather than puncture-wound osteomyelitis.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with long-standing diabetes has a chronic plantar ulcer with surrounding erythema and foul drainage. Cultures grow more than one organism, and treatment is complicated by resistance. Which of the following groups of organisms is most characteristic of diabetic foot infections?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mycobacteria in combination with dimorphic fungi

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neisseria species together with anaerobic spirochetes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Obligate anaerobes of the Bacteroides group alone

choices.label: D
choices.text: S. aureus, S. pyogenes, and gram-negative bacilli

explanation.summary: Diabetic foot infections are commonly caused by S. aureus, S. pyogenes, Pseudomonas, and other gram-negative bacilli, often together.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pseudomonas species are common causes of foot infections in diabetics along with S. aureus, S. pyogenes, and other gram-negative bacilli. In severe cases the bones and joints become infected as well. Mixed infections with multiple organisms are common and further complicate treatment, especially when multiple antibiotic-resistant strains are present.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Mycobacteria and dimorphic fungi cause chronic granulomatous disease, not typical diabetic foot infection.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Neisseria species and spirochetes are not the organisms recovered from diabetic foot ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anaerobes may participate, but infections are mixed rather than caused by Bacteroides alone.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Viridans streptococci are oral flora associated with endocarditis rather than foot ulcers.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 78-year-old nursing home resident with a chronic indwelling urinary catheter and several recent antibiotic courses develops fever and cloudy urine. Urine culture grows an oxidase-positive gram-negative rod that forms green-pigmented colonies. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: Catheterized, antibiotic-exposed patients are the ones who get opportunistic Pseudomonas urinary tract infections.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the community, E. coli and S. saprophyticus are by far the most common causes of urinary tract infection. In hospitals and long-term care, and in patients with pre-existing urinary tract problems or immunosuppression, opportunists such as Pseudomonas become more common, especially when a catheter and antibiotics are involved. The oxidase-positive gram-negative rod with green pigment confirms it here.

whyWrongByChoice.A: E. coli is the leading community uropathogen but ferments lactose and is oxidase negative.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Klebsiella pneumoniae is oxidase negative and does not produce green pigment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Proteus mirabilis is oxidase negative and characteristically raises urine pH rather than pigmenting colonies.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus saprophyticus is a gram-positive coccus, not a gram-negative rod.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an uncommon but recognized cause of infective endocarditis, which is most often caused by S. aureus and viridans streptococci. Which of the following patients is at greatest risk for endocarditis caused by Pseudomonas?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 29-year-old man who injects heroin intravenously

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 33-year-old woman in the second trimester of pregnancy

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 40-year-old woman with seasonal allergic rhinitis

choices.label: E
choices.text: A 61-year-old man with mild osteoarthritis of the knee

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas endocarditis occurs chiefly in people with damaged heart valves and in intravenous drug users.
explanation.whyCorrect: Patients with heart valve damage or who use intravenous drugs are at risk for infective endocarditis. S. aureus and viridans streptococci are the most common causes, but Pseudomonas can cause infective endocarditis as well, especially in intravenous drug users who repeatedly introduce environmental organisms directly into the bloodstream.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Normal pregnancy is not a described risk factor for Pseudomonas endocarditis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Allergic rhinitis carries no risk of bacterial seeding of cardiac valves.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Well-controlled hypertension alone does not damage valves or create a portal of entry.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease and confers no endocarditis risk.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 12-day-old neonate is admitted with tachypnea, grunting, and an infiltrate on chest radiograph. Which of the following organisms is among the most common causes of pneumonia in this age group?

explanation.summary: Group B streptococci and E. coli are the leading causes of pneumonia in neonates under four weeks of age.
explanation.whyCorrect: The common causes of community-acquired pneumonia vary sharply by age. In neonates younger than four weeks, group B streptococci and E. coli predominate. Pseudomonas does not appear on the age-based list of common community-acquired pneumonia pathogens at all; it becomes important in the hospital setting instead.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Chlamydia pneumoniae is associated with school-aged children and young adults.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Influenza virus is listed among the common causes in adults 65 and older.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mycoplasma is typical of older children and adults aged 18 to 40, not neonates.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pseudomonas is not among the common community-acquired pneumonia pathogens in any age group.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Pseudomonas accounts for a far greater share of hospital-acquired pneumonia than of community-acquired pneumonia. Which of the following combinations best explains this disproportionate rate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Airborne spread and an unusually potent protein exotoxin

choices.label: B
choices.text: High community carriage and efficient person-to-person spread

choices.label: C
choices.text: Loss of normal flora and formation of bacterial endospores

choices.label: D
choices.text: Poor host health, intrinsic resistance, and artificial surfaces

choices.label: E
choices.text: Seasonal outbreaks and brief survival in the environment

explanation.summary: Sick hosts, intrinsic antibiotic resistance, and growth on devices such as endotracheal tubes make Pseudomonas a hospital organism.
explanation.whyCorrect: The combination of poor health in hospitalized patients, intrinsic antibiotic resistance, and the ability of Pseudomonas to thrive on artificial surfaces such as an endotracheal tube contributes to its disproportionate rate in the healthcare setting. In hospitals, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, and members of the Enterobacteriaceae become the dominant causes of nosocomial bacterial infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Exotoxin A matters for tissue damage, but airborne spread is not how Pseudomonas pneumonia arises.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Pseudomonas is not carried as normal flora and does not spread efficiently person to person in the community.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pseudomonas does not form endospores.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The organism survives extremely well in the environment and is not a seasonal pathogen.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: In 2023, a nationwide outbreak was traced to contaminated artificial tears. Eighty-one patients across 18 states were infected, 14 lost vision, 4 required surgical removal of an eye, and 4 died of disseminated infection. Which of the following organisms was responsible?

explanation.summary: An extensively drug-resistant strain of Pseudomonas contaminated artificial tears and caused a fatal multistate outbreak in 2023.
explanation.whyCorrect: In 2023 EzriCare artificial tears were recalled after contamination with an extensively drug-resistant strain of Pseudomonas. In total 81 patients in 18 states were infected, 14 had vision loss, 4 required eye removal, and 4 died from dissemination. The episode illustrates both the organism's ability to thrive in products meant to be sterile and its drug resistance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acinetobacter causes hospital-acquired pneumonia and wound infection, not this ophthalmic product outbreak.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Burkholderia cepacia is a close relative that causes similar infections but was not the cause of this outbreak.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Serratia marcescens is listed among antibiotic-sensitive Enterobacteriaceae and was not implicated.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus aureus is a common eyelid and skin pathogen but was not the outbreak organism.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A microbiology technologist opening a stack of plates notes that one has a distinctive odor often likened to corn chips or fermented grapes. Which of the following organisms is classically described as smelling this way?

explanation.summary: Pseudomonas has a distinctive odor described as corn chips or fermented grapes, though smell is never a reliable identification method.
explanation.whyCorrect: The smell of Pseudomonas is distinct among bacteria. While most bacteria have an unpleasant generic odor, Pseudomonas species are described as smelling like Fritos corn chips or like fermented grapes or wine. The point is a mnemonic rather than a method: deliberately sniffing a potentially deadly pathogen is a terrible idea, and smell is not a good way to identify bacteria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acinetobacter is described by its non-pigmented, creamy colonies rather than a distinctive smell.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Escherichia coli has no such characteristic odor described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Klebsiella pneumoniae is not associated with a grape or corn chip odor.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus aureus is identified by its gram stain and catalase and coagulase reactions, not by odor.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Colonies of Pseudomonas aeruginosa growing on an agar plate most characteristically appear which of the following colors?

explanation.summary: Pyocyanin and pyoverdine give Pseudomonas colonies a blue-to-aqua, green-tinged appearance.
explanation.whyCorrect: P. aeruginosa produces two pigments, the blue pyocyanin and the yellow fluorescent pyoverdine. Because of these two pigments, colonies appear blue to aqua, and cultures are described as having an aqua or green color. The same pigments explain the green pus often seen with Pseudomonas infections.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Golden yellow colonies are classically associated with Staphylococcus aureus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Red pigmentation is not a described feature of Pseudomonas colonies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Colorless or creamy colonies describe Acinetobacter, which is non-pigmented.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Black colonies are not characteristic of this organism.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: Two gram-negative organisms resemble Pseudomonas aeruginosa so closely in epidemiology, patient population, and antibiotic resistance that they are studied alongside it and are not routinely distinguished from it by laboratory testing at this level. Which of the following pairs is it?

explanation.summary: Burkholderia cepacia and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia are the two close relatives of Pseudomonas that cause similar infections in similar patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Burkholderia cepacia and Stenotrophomonas maltophilia are very similar to Pseudomonas and cause similar infections, with similar epidemiology in each case. They are considered collectively with Pseudomonas, and students are not expected to differentiate them by laboratory identification or clinical presentation. Burkholderia cepacia also appears alongside P. aeruginosa among the multidrug-resistant causes of ventilator-associated pneumonia.

whyWrongByChoice.B: E. coli and Klebsiella are lactose-fermenting Enterobacteriaceae, readily separated from Pseudomonas.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Haemophilus and Legionella are respiratory pathogens unrelated to the Pseudomonas group.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neisseria and Moraxella are gram-negative cocci and diplococci with different disease patterns.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Salmonella and Shigella are non-lactose fermenters but are oxidase negative and cause enteric disease.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and hypertension is admitted to the intensive care unit after a major stroke and is intubated for mechanical ventilation. On ventilation day 5 she develops fever, increased respiratory effort, and purulent sputum, with tachypnea and bibasilar crackles. Endotracheal aspirate shows gram-negative bacilli that are oxidase positive and grow green colonies. Which of the following is the most likely organism?

explanation.summary: A ventilated ICU patient with an oxidase-positive, green-pigmented gram-negative bacillus has Pseudomonas ventilator-associated pneumonia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because the patient is ventilated and hospitalized, gram-negative bacilli such as Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter are the likely culprits, along with MRSA and members of the Enterobacteriaceae. Further laboratory testing showing oxidase positivity and green colonies confirms Pseudomonas, since Acinetobacter is oxidase negative and non-pigmented. Empiric antibiotics are then narrowed after sensitivity testing.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acinetobacter is a plausible ICU pathogen but is an oxidase-negative, non-pigmented coccobacillus.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Escherichia coli is oxidase negative and ferments lactose.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Klebsiella pneumoniae is oxidase negative and does not produce green pigment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Staphylococcus aureus is a gram-positive coccus, not a gram-negative bacillus.

questions.topicName: Pseudomonas species and other closely related bacteria

questions.stem: A 6-month-old with poor weight gain and recurrent respiratory infections is found to have an elevated sweat chloride concentration, and genetic testing confirms the diagnosis. The responsible gene defect follows which inheritance pattern and lies on which chromosome?

choices.label: E
choices.text: X-linked recessive, on the X chromosome

explanation.summary: Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive mutation of the CFTR gene on chromosome 7.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cystic fibrosis results from an autosomal recessive mutation in the CFTR gene, which encodes the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator and sits on chromosome 7. The mutation impairs chloride and water transport across epithelial cells, producing thick, sticky mucus in the lungs, pancreas, intestines, and reproductive tract. Screening tests are followed by confirmatory sweat chloride measurement and genetic testing for the CFTR mutation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Neither the dominant pattern nor chromosome 17 matches the CFTR gene.
whyWrongByChoice.B: The inheritance is recessive, not dominant, and the gene is not on chromosome 4.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Mitochondrial inheritance would be maternal and does not apply to CFTR.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Cystic fibrosis affects males and females equally and is not X-linked.
